visualLimitations: Columns, overhead lights, full side/south walls, ramp, barrier and fire door are missing. The short northwest wall return and open cutaway edges do not establish a complete enclosed facility.
Uniform concrete dominates the enlarged footprint. Repeated identical cars, stops and bay markings make it look like an expanded parking-chip demonstration rather than a finished garage.
The two north-wall light features leave the middle and southern areas without visible lighting infrastructure.

Two broad longitudinal aisles and a southern connector are visually legible, but lack circulation cues and a defined entrance. Their apparent clearance does not prove vehicle turning, door clearance or engine walking.
evidence: Viewed tiledata/modern-city/parking-wide/scene.png and parking-approved/scene.png directly; read harness-data/modern-chipset/parking-wide/plan.md. This verdict independently assesses the new arrangement.
The 416×288 expansion visibly contains two banks of six bays, with three occupied bays per bank: six cars and six empty spaces.
North-wall panels form a continuous band. Bay separators and terminal lines align; no conspicuous broken joins, floor patch seams or repeated internal wall/return artifacts are visible.

Occupied bays preserve the small scene's car-to-stop relationship: the right-facing car meets and partly occludes the stop area. No obvious new floating gap or displaced stop is visible; occupied stops are partly hidden.

Cars retain visible roof surfaces and side profiles, consistent with the north wall's raised face and the source scene's shallow 3/4 presentation. No rotated or differently scaled car disrupts that perspective.
The plan specifies 96px longitudinal aisles and a 48px southern connector. The image shows these as continuous open floor regions, supporting a coherent static pedestrian layout.

Parking identity is immediate from cars, white bay lines and stops. Underground or enclosed-garage identity remains weak because structural enclosure and supporting fixtures are absent. Runtime traversability requires a separate supervisor check.
